# OmniRoute — The Free AI Gateway **Created by [Diego Souza](https://github.com/diegosouzapw)**
## Free Tokens a Month: ~11.3B as Others Count · ~90M Real
> **~11.3B free tokens / month**
> counted the way other catalogs count: every row added up, ended offers included > > **~90M real today**
> each shared quota counted once: what you can actually use > > **Everything here is free. No paywall.**
> ★ [Like it? Star us on GitHub](https://github.com/cheaper-inference/OmniRoute) Other catalogs charge from US$ 19 a year to US$ 49 for lifetime access to live data. Here everything is free. Prices checked on 2026-11-18. Catalog last audited on 2026-11-23. [How we count →](docs/reference/FREE_TIERS.md#how-we-count) > **Bring your own provider accounts.** These are third-party free tiers, not a token grant from OmniRoute. Sign up, get credentials where a provider asks for them, and connect the ones you can use. Each provider sets its own limits, availability and terms. > > Stacking free tiers by hand means dozens of SDKs, dozens of rate limits and no clear idea of what you have left. OmniRoute keeps 214 catalog rows with free access and computes the real figure from 12 pools with a published quota, each shared pool counted once. Quotas that only open after a regional identity check (today, ModelScope) are shown apart, +~6M behind regional identity verification, and never added to the real figure. What is left shows up on the dashboard (`/dashboard/free-tiers`). > Animated summary of the live `/dashboard/free-tiers` page. How each figure is counted: **[docs/reference/FREE_TIERS.md#how-we-count](docs/reference/FREE_TIERS.md#how-we-count)**. > > Catalog last audited on 2026-11-23. The figures move both ways. A provider ends a free tier and the real number drops. A new one lands and it climbs. We publish what the catalog computes, never a rounded-up best case.

## Install, connect a provider, then route through one endpoint ```bash # After connecting a provider, create your OmniRoute key in Dashboard → API Keys: curl http://localhost:20128/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_OMNIROUTE_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"auto","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello!"}]}' ``` `auto` needs an eligible route. A fresh installation can have no eligible keyless targets, and a keyless provider may reject third-party clients. Providers marked `tos: avoid`, including Kiro, are excluded from automatic routing by default; connecting an account does not override that setting. See the [Free Tiers Guide](docs/getting-started/FREE-TIERS-GUIDE.md) before choosing a provider. Copy-paste quickstart scripts for **Python, Node.js, PHP and cURL**: [`examples/quickstart/`](examples/quickstart/). Step-by-step version: [Quick Start](#quick-start).

## Combos: the flagship 1. **Start with `auto`.** Set the model in your OpenAI-compatible client. OmniRoute builds a virtual combo from connected providers and scores candidates live. 2. **Save a combo for more control.** Choose a name, target list and strategy, then use that name as the model. The strategy sets which target goes first and how the rest are tried. A combo routes across models automatically. On quota exhaustion, provider failure or model lockout, it tries the next eligible, healthy target. ### Zero-config: just use `auto` ```bash curl http://localhost:20128/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}' ``` Variants tune the weights. Last-known-good routing stays with the last successful provider until it fails, then rescores. `auto/fast` and `auto/cheap` express preferences without guaranteeing the fastest or cheapest model. | Model ID | Behavior | | :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `auto` | Balanced default weights. | | `auto/fast` | Favors low latency and provider health. | | `auto/cheap` | Favors lower catalog prices. | | `auto/coding` | Quality-first weights for code generation. | | `auto/smart` | Quality-first weights with 10% exploration (default 5%). | | `auto/lkgp` | Explicit last-known-good routing with the same weights as `auto`. | | `auto/subscription` | Uses only live-verified plan quota. Returns HTTP 503 when none is available and avoids billed fallback. | | `auto/thrifty` | Plan → keyless → free → cheap → premium. May reach billed models and returns to the plan when quota and cooldown allow. | | `auto/offline` | Favors quota and rate-limit headroom. Requests still go to your providers. | | `auto/chaos` | One model per provider in parallel, up to five by default or ten when configured. One upstream call per model. Returns the top-ranked reply or the last successful panel reply if the top model fails. Use `fusion` to synthesize replies with a judge. | Category and optional tier examples include `auto/coding:fast`, `auto/coding:free`, `auto/reasoning:pro` and `auto/vision`. If no connected candidate matches, the request returns HTTP 503 and the pool stays narrow. [Auto-Combo guide](./docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md) · [Subscription-first routing](./docs/routing/SUBSCRIPTION_LADDER.md) ### Or build your own: 22 routing strategies ```bash omniroute combo create my-pool --strategy fill-first \ --models "provider-a/model-1,provider-b/model-2" ``` The CLI accepts 15 of 22 strategies. The dashboard and combos API accept all 22. | Strategy | Behavior | | :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `auto` | Rank candidates live with the 16-factor Auto-Combo scorer. | | `cache-optimized` | Prefer the account likely to hold the prompt prefix in cache. | | `context-optimized` | Try the largest known context window first. | | `context-relay` | Keep your order and pass a conversation summary when switching accounts. | | `cost-optimized` | Sort by catalog input-token price, unknowns last. Final request cost can differ. | | `expiry-first` | Spend quota likely to expire, highest leftover per hour until reset first. | | `fill-first` | Stay on the first available target until it runs out or fails, then move on. | | `fusion` | Query a panel in parallel and have a judge synthesize one answer. | | `headroom` | Choose the most free capacity across 5-hour and weekly windows. | | `jev` | TypeSafe Jev picks which entries in your ranked list run. Turn on `COMBO_JEV_STRATEGY_ENABLED` to send an excerpt per request and use paid TypeSafe calls. With it off, your order applies. | | `least-used` | Pick the target with the fewest recorded requests in this combo. | | `lkgp` | Try the last successful provider first, otherwise keep your order. | | `p2c` | Sample two targets and pick by success rate and latency. | | `pipeline` | Feed each step's output into the next target in sequence and return only the final answer. | | `priority` | Try targets in your order. Session stickiness preserves it. | | `quota-weighted` | Skip exhausted accounts and draw by leftover quota and in-flight load. | | `random` | Shuffle for each request. The same first target can repeat. | | `reset-aware` | Score remaining quota and time to reset across session and weekly windows. | | `reset-window` | Try the account whose quota window resets soonest. | | `round-robin` | Rotate in order, three successes per target by default. | | `strict-random` | Deal from a shuffled deck so each target leads once before repeats. | | `weighted` | Draw a first target by weight and keep the rest as fallbacks. The split is statistical. Use `round-robin` for strict rotation. | Quota strategies use live data where providers report it, including 5-hour and weekly subscription windows. `fusion` and `pipeline` make multiple upstream calls per request. The 16-factor scorer uses quota, health, cost, latency, task fit, stability, tier priority, tier affinity, specificity match, context affinity, cache affinity, session availability, reset-window affinity, connection density, quality and reliability. Weights vary by profile. Cache affinity, reset-window affinity and reliability have zero weight by default. [Scoring factors](./docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md#how-it-works-persisted-auto-combos) In a saved combo with `strategy: "auto"`, `config.routerStrategy` selects `rules`, `score`, `cost` (`eco`), `latency` (`fast`), `sla-aware` (`sla`), `lkgp`, `nadir` or `decision`. [Auto router strategies](./docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md#auto-router-strategies) ### Resilience is built in: 3 independent layers Failures are handled at three scopes, so one bad model does not take down its account, and one bad account does not take down its provider. #### If a whole provider is down The **provider circuit breaker** opens after 8 (OAuth) or 12 (API key) failures with status 408, 500, 502, 503 or 504. Combos skip that provider while it is open. After 60 s or 30 s, one probe request decides whether it closes. #### If one key or account is rate-limited The **connection cooldown** benches only that connection, with exponential backoff from 5 s (OAuth) or 3 s (API key). Other keys for the same provider keep serving. #### If one model is refused The **model lockout** blocks only that model on that connection after a per-model 429, 404 or access denial. Other models on the same connection keep serving. Banned, expired and out-of-credit connections are terminal states, not cooldowns: they wait for you to fix them. [Auto-Combo engine](docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md) · [Resilience guide](docs/architecture/RESILIENCE_GUIDE.md)

## OmniRoute Radar Radar is the live, signed copy of the free-tier catalog above, and it is free for everyone. There is no paywall and no waiting period. It is opt-in and GET-only. The OmniRoute client sends nothing to Radar: no prompts, traffic, provider configuration or usage telemetry. The numbers above come from the catalog shipped with this release. Radar can show newer data between releases. New free offers and promotions are added every week. Watch the real number grow on the Radar. **[OmniRoute Radar →](docs/frameworks/RADAR.md)**

## Compatible CLIs & Coding Agents The dashboard catalog lists **39 integrations** (28 coding tools and 11 agents). The CLI manifest adds Gemini CLI, which launches with `omniroute run`, and four tools it can only detect. Of all of them, **8** launch with `omniroute run`, **12** can be set up with `omniroute configure`, and **16** have a dedicated `setup-*` command. Pick the path that matches what you want. ### If you want to launch a tool in one command `omniroute run` starts the tool with OmniRoute's URL and key in its environment. Nothing is written to disk.

```bash omniroute run claude --model openai/gpt-5.4 # Claude Code omniroute run codex --model glm/glm-5.2 # Codex CLI omniroute run aider --model glm/glm-5.2 -- --message "reply OK" omniroute run goose --model glm/glm-5.2 omniroute run opencode --model glm/glm-5.2 -- run "reply OK" omniroute run qwen --model glm/glm-5.2 -- -p "reply OK" omniroute run gemini --model glm/glm-5.2 -- --skip-trust -p "reply OK" omniroute setup-whycodes && omniroute run whycodes --model glm/glm-5.2 # Or pick provider and model interactively and write the tool's own config: omniroute configure codex # also: claude opencode qwen aider goose gemini whycodes cline continue kilo 5dive ``` Every command honors the active remote context (`omniroute connect `). `--dry-run` prints the exact env and args without running anything, and `--api-key-env NAME` keeps the key out of your shell history. Qwen Code and Gemini CLI run in a temporary home that is deleted on exit. WhyCodes reads its provider only from `config.toml`, so run `setup-whycodes` once before `run whycodes`. → [CLI Integrations](docs/guides/CLI-INTEGRATIONS.md) ### If you want OmniRoute to write the tool's config `omniroute configure ` lets you pick a provider and model, then writes the tool's own config file.
